newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki nudges higher on tailwind from Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki nudges higher on tailwind from Wall Street.

text.p: Shares edged up on Wednesday in moderately active trading with firm showings by Nokia and banking shares. Players were encouraged by the surge of the U.S. stock market on Tuesday, brokers said.
The HEX index nudged ahead 0.24 percent to 2,191.40. Volume was fair at 358 million markka.
Brokers said Helsinki could extend gains on Thursday if Wall Street keeps its upward trend.
"The telecoms sector looks strong, and it could take the market somewhat higher tomorrow," one broker said.
Telecoms major Nokia closed rose 0.80 markka to 202.30 in modest trade, matching its early dealings in New York. Nokia accounted for 16 percent of total bourse volume.
Banks, particularly Merita, remained in focus amid talk of possible restructuring in the sector, brokers said. Merita A added 0.20 markka to close active trade at 10.80.
Pharmaceutical wholesaler Tamro ended 0.30 markka higher at 34.30 after hitting a new five-year high 34.80 on overseas demand sparked by the group's recent foreign acquisitions, brokers said.

Steel group Rautaruukki ended 0.10 markka higher at 41.30 after touching a 22-month high 43.00 markka in fair trade fuelled by a news report suggesting that British Steel might be interested in discussing partnership with Rautaruukki.

Forestries rose slightly, but trade in paper industry shares was thin and dampened by the sector's uncertain outlook. UPM-Kymmene ended flat at 96.50 markka, and Enso put on 0.20 to end at 36.70. Metsa-Serla rose 0.40 markka to 30.00.
Chemicals group Kemira fell 0.40 markka to 52.50 in active trade ahead of January-August results due on Thursday.
